generic_sampling_rules.int_pk: Sequential integers starting at 1; never NULL; unique per table; generated PKs start above the compact max so no post-hoc offset is needed.
generic_sampling_rules.int_fk: Sample from parent key pool (compact + generated parent keys); 5-30% NULL when nullable; ensure some parent rows have no children; FK values must reference the final written PKs.
generic_sampling_rules.text_name: Draw from a small pool of realistic names; allow 20-50% duplicate share on DISTINCT columns; near-variants (case/whitespace) for equality literals.
generic_sampling_rules.text_enum: Draw uniformly from the enumerated value list; allow case near-variants where listed.
generic_sampling_rules.text_free: Short realistic strings; allow NULL only when the column is in null_targets.
generic_sampling_rules.real_numeric: Draw from the observed min/max range; integer-valued when statistics show integer-like values.
generic_sampling_rules.null_rule: Plant NULLs only in columns listed in null_targets; every listed nullable column gets at least one NULL row per instance; NULL share follows compact DB share (5-30% typical); NOT NULL/PK columns never NULL; planted NULLs are never replaced to satisfy a rule.

generation_specification.uncertainty: Original Ship has 9 rows but only 8 Ship_ID/Name values shown; captain has 7 rows with 5 distinct Ship_ID. Nullability of captain.Ship_ID is inferred from the null_rows atomic operation; all other columns are treated as NOT NULL for NULL-planting purposes. Ship.Type, Ship.Class, Ship.Flag and Ship.Built_Year are single/two-value observations from a tiny sample and are kept as soft hints, not hard domain constraints. No date pairs or calculated columns exist, so no order or formula rules beyond range/enum. FK values must be chosen after final PK assignment (generated PKs above compact max) so no post-hoc offset is applied.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback reports integrity.fk_violations = 3 and validity.invalid = 2 with reason 'new_integrity_failures'. The writer (writer.py) opens the copy with 'pragma foreign_keys = OFF' and never re-enables it, and instance.py's fill_foreign_keys_consistently draws FK values from _parent_pool which includes generated parent keys, but writer._fresh_pk_offset shifts every generated PK by the compact max AFTER the FK values were already chosen. So a generated captain.Ship_ID pointing at a generated Ship.Ship_ID (e.g. 3) is written as 3+offset while the Ship row's PK is also shifted, but the FK column is not shifted, producing dangling references. This is a real construction bug, not a query-equivalence artifact.
issues.requested_revision: Make FK values consistent with the shifted PKs: either (a) apply the same _fresh_pk_offset to FK columns that reference a table whose PK was offset, or (b) choose generated PKs above the compact max inside instance.py (as the writer docstring claims) so no post-hoc shift is needed, and remove the shift in writer.py. Also enable 'pragma foreign_keys = ON' before commit (or run a post-insert FK check) so violations are caught rather than silently written.

issues.evidence: The NULL rule requires that NOT NULL / PK columns never get NULL and that every nullable column gets at least one NULL per instance. Execution feedback shows NULLs planted in Ship.Built_Year, Ship.Class, Ship.Flag, Ship.Name, Ship.Type, captain.Class, captain.Name, captain.Rank, captain.age — but the schema declares only captain.Ship_ID as nullable (all other columns are NOT NULL in the DDL; Ship.Built_Year is REAL NOT NULL by default in SQLite only if declared, but here it is declared without NOT NULL, so it is technically nullable). More importantly, the specification's null_targets is only ['captain.Ship_ID'], and the atomic operations only flag captain.Ship_ID null_rows. _plant_nulls in instance.py plants NULLs in every column where cm.notnull is False, which for this schema includes Ship.Name, Ship.Type, Ship.Class, Ship.Flag, Ship.Built_Year, captain.Name, captain.Class, captain.Rank, captain.age. This contradicts the specification's null_targets and the 'none (NOT NULL column)' target for captain.Captain_ID, and it injects NULLs into columns the spec treats as populated (e.g. Ship.Type='Panamax', Ship.Flag in {Panama,Malta}).
issues.requested_revision: Restrict _plant_nulls to columns listed in spec['null_targets'] (or to columns whose domain descriptor carries a null_share), and never plant NULLs in columns the specification constrains by enum/range unless the spec explicitly marks them nullable. Update the specification's null_targets to match the intended nullable set, and make the sampler respect it.

issues.evidence: The specification's semantic_rules_and_formulas include Ship.Type IN ('Panamax'), Ship.Class IN ('KR','GL'), Ship.Flag IN ('Panama','Malta'), Ship.Built_Year BETWEEN 1997.0 AND 1998.0, captain.Class IN (...), captain.Rank IN (...), captain.age BETWEEN 18 AND 80. The supporting_evidence section states these are inferred from 'shown' rows only ('All 8 shown Ship rows have Type=Panamax', etc.), and the uncertainty field admits 'Original Ship has 9 rows but only 8 Ship_ID/Name values shown'. These are therefore uncertain patterns, not established rules: a single-value enum (Ship.Type='Panamax') and a two-value range (Built_Year 1997-1998) are almost certainly artifacts of the small sample, not true domain constraints. Treating them as hard rules collapses value variation (e.g. Ship.Type can only ever be 'Panamax', Built_Year only 1997/1998), which is exactly the kind of over-constraint that makes generated instances unrepresentative.
issues.requested_revision: Downgrade the single-value and two-value 'IN'/'BETWEEN' formulas to soft hints (e.g. keep the observed values in the pool but allow additional realistic values), or mark them explicitly as 'uncertain' and exclude them from hard domain enforcement. Keep only rules with clear evidence (e.g. captain.age 18-80 is plausible; Ship_ID > 0 and Captain_ID > 0 are structural).

issues.evidence: The specification's per_column_exceptions for captain.age require 'qualifying_rows: >= 2 per group with different values', and the atomic operation rows_with_different_values targets '>= 2 per group with different values'. instance.py's _distinct_per_group only acts when dom.get('distinct_per_group') is set, and spec.py's load_specification never sets 'distinct_per_group' from the per_column_exceptions (it only maps values, comparison_values, duplicate_share, group_sizes, null_share). The default spec does set distinct_per_group for captain.age, but load_specification overwrites/merges only the listed keys, so when a specification.json is present the distinct_per_group hint is lost. Additionally _distinct_per_group groups by the first FK column of the table, which for captain is Ship_ID — but captain.Ship_ID is also the column being NULL-planted, so groups keyed on NULL are not meaningful.
issues.requested_revision: In spec.py, map the 'rows_with_different_values' / 'qualifying_rows' target to a distinct_per_group flag (or equivalent) so the instance builder enforces it. In instance.py, group by the FK column only for non-NULL FK values, and ensure at least two distinct captain.age values per non-NULL Ship_ID group.

issues.evidence: The specification's ties_for_order_limit targets for Ship.Ship_ID and Ship.Built_Year require tie_at_rank [1] on COUNT(*) DESC, and for captain.Name require ORDER(captain.name, ASC) with no LIMIT. instance.py's _apply_group_sizes realises group sizes 1,2,3 by repeating values, but it does not guarantee a tie at rank 1 for COUNT(*) DESC (i.e. two groups with the same maximum count). The construction_pairs feedback shows only 15/49 separated, and no group-level breakdown is provided, so the tie targets are unverified. This is a coverage gap rather than a hard error, but it means the specified tie patterns are not demonstrably realised.
issues.requested_revision: Add an explicit tie-realisation step for columns flagged with ties_for_order_limit: ensure at least two groups share the maximum COUNT(*) (for DESC tie_at_rank [1]) and, for captain.Name, ensure the ASC ordering is exercised. Report per-group construction results so the tie targets can be verified.

issues.evidence: The specification's comparison_boundary targets for Ship.Flag require values ['Panama','panama','Malta','malta'] and for captain.Class require ['Armed schooner','armed schooner'], and captain.Rank requires ['Midshipman','midshipman']. spec.py's load_specification maps 'comparison_values' to d['variants'], but the default spec already lists variants for these columns; however, EnumSampler draws uniformly from values+variants, so the case near-variants are present but the duplicate_share (20-50%) is applied by _apply_duplicate_share only when dom.get('dup_share') is set — and load_specification sets dup_share only when 'duplicate_share' is in targets, which it is for Ship.Flag, Ship.Name, captain.Class. So the duplicate share is applied, but the comparison_boundary values are only guaranteed if the variants list is populated. For Ship.Flag the default spec has variants ['panama','malta'], so this is likely fine; but the specification's per_column_exceptions for Ship.Flag list values ['Panama','panama','Malta','malta'] as the target, and load_specification's 'values' mapping would set d['values'] to those four, then EnumSampler would treat 'panama' and 'malta' as separate values rather than variants — which is acceptable but changes the intended distribution. This is a minor consistency issue.
issues.requested_revision: Clarify in spec.py whether comparison_boundary values are enum values or case variants, and ensure the sampler produces both the canonical and near-variant forms with the intended duplicate share. Add a construction check that the comparison_boundary values actually appear in generated rows.
